title: Creation of a digital surface data set of transport infrastructure in Luxembourg
description: The spatial database created in this project lays the foundation to put all mobility data, existing and future, into the context of the multimodal transport network. This helps automating the interpretation of incoming data and constitutes the first step of taking the ODM from a data aggregator to a "digital twin" (or, more accurately, a "digital shadow") of the transport system. By that, we mean a digital copy of the mobility system that updates autonomously with every new observation arriving from the real system

title: ESPON Mapping Mediterranean Cooperation Networks and Governance - MedCoopNet
description: The Targeted Analysis will contribute to understanding the Mediterranean emerging geography in terms of its delineations, functional and cooperation arrangements, involved actors and coherence with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), providing evidence to inform new governance mechanisms and consolidate the existing ones. Specifically, the Targeted Analysis aims to provide evidence on cooperation dynamics, their spatial and thematic distribution; their spatial and thematic overlaps and potential spatial and thematic gaps; their institutional and funding foundations and their effects on sustainable development in the functional area.

description: This targeted analysis aims to carry out a territorial analysis of the North Sea Rhine Mediterranean Corridor and deliver a sound and evidence-based foundation for developing a common spatial and governance approach for the NSMED Corridor, potentially serving as a model for other trans-European corridors. title: RFP 250029 - CALL FOR TENDER – PROCUREMENT OF PAPER BOOKS
description: The University of Luxembourg is launching this call for tenders with the objective of concluding a Framework Agreement for the procurement of books in paper format, including academic publications and conference proceedings, to support its teaching and research activities. The publications shall cover a wide array of disciplines such as: - Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine - Law, Economics and Finance - Education & Social Work, Behavioural & Cognitive Sciences, Humanities, Social Sciences, Geography & Spatial Planning - Security, Reliability and Trust - Systems Biomedicine - Contemporary and Digital History - European Law - Socio-Environmental Systems. This list is non-exhaustive, and the University reserves the right to request documentation in additional subject areas as necessary. Excluded from the scope of this contract are publications issued by the University of Luxembourg as well as works that are exclusively distributed by the publishers. The Framework Agreement shall encompass the following services and supplies: - Provision of bibliographic and pricing information for requested titles; - Submission of price quotations upon request; - Supply and delivery of books to the University; - Issuance of invoices in compliance with the University's administrative requirements; - Participation in an annual performance review meeting with University representatives; - Provision and maintenance of an online ordering platform that enables University staff to search for titles, submit orders, and track deliveries. This platform is an essential component of the present procurement procedure and it must be operational throughout the duration of the agreement. The present call for tenders is intended to result in the conclusion of a Framework Agreement for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable three (3) times for successive one (1) year periods (1+1+1+1), subject to the University’s decision and performance evaluation. The Framework Agreement will be concluded with one (1) contractor per lot. No reopening of competition shall occur during the validity of the agreement.

title: Acquisition d’un système complet d’échosondeur multifaisceaux
description: Un système hydrographique multifaisceaux de dernière génération est recherché pour la mesure précise des fonds aquatiques. L’objectif est l’acquisition d’un système intégré composé d’un sonar multifaisceaux, d’un logiciel d’acquisition performant, ainsi que d’un système de navigation inertielle (INS) assisté par GNSS. Le système doit répondre aux exigences les plus élevées en matière de précision, de stabilité et de flexibilité, et être adapté à une utilisation dans des environnements maritimes et limniques exigeants (Moselle). Les spécifications techniques ci-dessous définissent les exigences minimales pour le système à fournir. Les soumissionnaires sont invités à détailler dans leur offre en quoi leur solution répond ou dépasse les caractéristiques demandées. Un seul fabricant doit être choisi pour l’ensemble du système, comprenant le sonar multifaisceaux, le logiciel d’acquisition et le système INS.

title: ESPON Baltic ReSeaLand - Territorial Resilience of Land and Maritime Space in the Baltic Sea Region
description: This targeted analysis aims to strengthen the evidence base for resilience-oriented territorial governance in the Baltic Sea Region by developing a comprehensive analytical framework for assessing and operationalising territorial resilience across both terrestrial and maritime spaces. ESPON Baltic ReSeaLand will operationalise territorial resilience in the BSR through a set of indicators to measure adaptive capacity, vulnerability, and exposure across both land and sea; territorial analyses highlighting resilience patterns, hotspots, and critical areas requiring targeted interventions; and methodological guidelines to integrate resilience considerations into spatial planning, policy design, and cross-sectoral governance. It will also produce actionable, evidence-based recommendations enabling integrated, proactive, and strategic planning across terrestrial and maritime spaces.

title: Strengthening smaller and medium-sized towns – together in Europe (SMTs)
description: This territorial study is being carried out at the request of the German Federal Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building (BMWSB), with the intention to shift more attention of territorial policies to small and medium-sized towns as interfaces between urban and rural areas in national and European strategies for urban and spatial development. Stakeholders engaged in spatial and urban planning and related policy development shall benefit from the findings of this study by getting a clearer understanding of the roles that small and medium-sized towns play in the everyday life of people, and therefore the consideration they should be given in strategies and funding programmes to achieve a balanced and cohesive territorial development, both in Germany and across Europe.
